item.title: Informing patients about diagnostic imaging: can we do better? - Radiology Cafe
item.description: I once got asked by the duty radiologist: "Does the patient know they are coming down for a scan?". The question was initially puzzling, as it seemed to have an obvious answer… but do we always inform patients appropriately of decisions around diagnostic imaging?

item.title: Radiology Cafe interview on RadCast - Radiology Cafe
item.description: Dr Christopher Clarke is interviewed on the RadCast radiology podcast about Radiology Cafe. He talks about when and how the website was created, his mission and touches on the role of social media in radiology.

item.title: A brief history of radiology - Radiology Cafe
item.description: Blog post covering a brief history of radiological advances covering X-rays, tomography, ultrasound (US), computed tomography (CT) and interventional radiology (IR). Image of the first X-ray ever taken and key figures in radiology over the last century or so.

item.title: New edition of CXR book released - Radiology Cafe
item.description: I am delighted to announce that the 2nd edition of Chest X-rays for Medical Students is published on 12th March 2020. This new edition includes significant revisions, improved annotations, expanded pathologies, and numerous additional high-quality images. A comprehensive one-stop guide to learning CXR interpretation.

item.title: Video tutorials from Radiology Masters - Radiology Cafe
item.description: Blog post shout out to the Radiology Masters team and a brief overview of their radiology video teaching resources for radiology trainees in this COVID-19 lockdown time.

item.title: Digestive system tube map - Radiology Cafe
item.description: A map of the human digestive system in the style of the London Underground Tube map, complete with stations, multiple lines and lots of style! Inspired from the original work by Jack Anderson.

item.title: FRCR Physics Notes 3rd Edition - Radiology Cafe
item.description: FRCR Physics Notes: Medical imaging physics for the First FRCR examination is out now on Amazon in paperback. This is a massive update to the well established FRCR physics revision notes at Radiology Cafe. We have been working tirelessly over the last year to update the text, but more importantly release it as a paperback so trainees can annotate and flick through as they revise.
